verdicts.fix: عُطْلَة is feminine, so 'was' is usually كَانَتْ (كَانَ is possible but less usual). Before al- its sukūn turns into i: كَانَتِ الْعُطْلَة.

verdicts.reason: Real: عُطْلَة is a majāzī (grammatical, non-living) feminine; when it follows the verb directly, classical and modern grammars allow both تأنيث and تذكير of the verb (يجوز الوجهان مع المؤنث المجازي), feminine being the usual form. Calling كَانَ 'wrong' breaks the owner's guiding rule in DECISIONS.md ('where both forms are good, the card says better / usually, not wrong', applied in R3-55). The softened wording keeps كَانَتْ as the taught form and is accurate.
